data.title: Canonicals Interview Process
data.author: dijit
data.article_summary: 本文作者在2024年离开Google后开始寻找新工作，并申请了Canonical公司的一个高级职位。申请过程非常繁琐，首先需要回答一些关于高中成绩和大学学历的奇怪问题。由于作者没有特别关注高中排名，首次申请被拒。后来，在一些现任员工建议下，他虚构了成绩，才通过初筛。接下来是提交长达21页的PDF回答38个问题，并进行心理测试，包括智力测试和行为评估。智力测试类似逻辑题，而行为评估基于过时的DISC理论。技术面试内容较浅，多为开放性讨论，而非深入技术问题。HR面试则是常规的STAR问题，但面试官无视了作者之前提交的详细书面回答，令其感到不被尊重。整个过程让作者感到困惑和不满。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Canonical公司面试过程的争议

不同观点：
• 部分面试者认为Canonical的面试过程过于冗长且怪异，尤其是涉及到高中相关问题，令人感到不适。例如，retrobox和arp242提到他们在面试中遇到奇怪的气氛，并选择退出或感到不满。
• artyom指出面试过程不仅漫长，还包括无解释的拒绝，以及无意义的心理测评，质疑HR和整个流程的有效性。
• 一些评论者如tkzed49、Lu2025和Bendy聚焦于Canonical的创始人Shuttleworth，批评其行为自大和不专业，认为公司文化可能存在问题。
• bananapub和hamidr讨论了Canonical如何在薪酬和开源软件项目的名声之间取得平衡，质疑这种面试过程是否可持续。

补充讨论：
• vkaku提到现代技术如生成式AI如何使针对特定公司量身定制申请变得更容易，从而削弱了这些评估的初衷和意义。
• jofla_net和hamidr从更广泛的角度讨论了这种面试过程在其他大公司中也可能存在，并认为这种官僚主义和筛选过程让人感到无力和沮丧。
• 争议的焦点主要在于Shuttleworth在最终面试阶段的角色及其对整个面试过程的影响，以及这种冗长且复杂的招聘流程是否合理有效。

总结：评论者普遍对面试过程中的不透明、冗长和创始人的行为表示不满，同时对现代技术如何影响传统招聘评估方法提出了质疑。

44149549.article_content:
Context
I
left Google
in April 2024, and have thus
been casually looking for a new job during 2024. A good friend of mine is currently working
at
Canonical
, and he told me that it's quite a nice
company with a great working environment. Unfortunately,
the internet is full of people who had a poor experience:
Glassdoor
shows that only 15% had a positive interview experience,
famous internet denizens like
sara
rambled on the topic,
reddit
,
hacker
news
,
indeed
and
blind
all say it's terrible, â¦ but the idea of being decently paid to do security
work on a popular Linux distribution was really appealing to me.
First application
I first applied there in October 2023. Canonical's
careers'
website
asks a bunch of odd questions like:
How did you perform in mathematics at high school?
How did you perform in your native language at high school?
Please share your rationale or evidence for the high school performance
selections above. Make reference to provincial, state or nation-wide scoring
systems, rankings, or recognition awards, or to competitive or selective
college entrance results such as SAT or ACT scores, JAMB, matriculation
results, IB results etc. We recognise every system is different but we will
ask you to justify your selections above.
What was your bachelor's university degree result, or expected result if you
have not yet graduated? Please include the grading system to help us
understand your result e.g. â85 out of 100â, â2:1 (Grading system: first
class, 2:1, 2:2, third class)â or âGPA score of 3.8/4.0 (predicted)â. We have
hired outstanding individuals who did not attend or complete university. If
this describes you, please continue with your application and enter âno
degreeâ.
As I was applying for a
senior position
, and because there was no such thing as
ranking in my entire scholarship, I didn't think much about this, and wrote
that I wasn't bad at school, and that there was no ranking. I got instantly
rejected. I asked around, and some Canonical employees reached out to me on
mastodon
to tell me that I should lie on
this step of the hiring process, as people who aren't in the top 10% in
high-school are automatically rejected. So I made things up, and didn't get
rejected this time.
I then got an email about the "written interview", asking me to provide my
answers to
38 questions
in a PDF.
It took me a couple of hours to write it down, boiling down to 21 pages of
text. Once sent, I was asked to do
modern
phrenology
"psychometric
assessments" from
Thomas
. The first one is called the
General Intelligence Assessment, and features with questions like those:
"Bob isn't as fast as Carl" â Who is the fastest? Carl or Bob?
"a B f H" vs "k b j z" â how many letters in common? (1)
Given 3 numbers, find the bigger and smaller, which one is the farthest from the middle one?
Given a group of 3 words, which one has nothing to do with the 2 other?
Given a pair of letter "R", with some rotated and some mirrored, how many are
only rotated?
The second one is the Behavioural Assessment, and is based on
picking "the
word that corresponds the most to your personality and the one that corresponds
the least"
for 30 minutes. Their
"methodology" is based on the
DISC
assessment
from 1928 which is
completely made-up pseudo-science. Heck, even their
brochure
only has 5 references with none from after 1957, and the 5 mentioned "studies" don't
have sources, data, details, â¦ This made me equally amused and worried.
The technical interviews ("Ubuntu Skills Interview", "Security Skills
Interview", "General Management Skills Interview") felt a bit empty
content-wise, and sounded more like some random conversation with open-source
enthusiast people at a bar. The only technical questions I remember were "What's your
favourite git command" and "Can you tell me about Ubuntu packaging". Keep in
mind that the position I was applying for was "Ubuntu Engineering Manager", so
I was expecting a lot of technical questions. Don't get me wrong, the
conversations were really nice, and I really liked the reflections on
Canonical's positions and philosophy.
In December, I had an HR interview with a "Talent Science Partner", which was a
regular bland
STAR
questionnaire. Here is some feedback from the interviewer: "In the first 5
minutes of the call, I asked them about their biggest achievement at NBS and
they replied "Apparently you haven't read my 20-pages written interview". I
then explained to him that I have to ask the same questions to all candidates
and they offered me a terse answer." What's the point of asking for an
extensive written interview with those very same questions,
only for it to be completely ignored? It felt disrespectful to me.
Also, amusingly "During our interview, they will [sic.] be typing away.", so
candidates aren't expected to take notes. I was simply writing the questions
down, as well as some of my answers, likely the very same thing that the
interviewer was doing.

data.title: Photos taken inside musical instruments
data.author: worik
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章内容、图片效果及相关技术方法的评论与讨论

不同观点：
• [susam] 提出了一个游戏：通过开发者工具使文本不可见，然后猜测图片代表的乐器，并分享了自己的得分（5/8）。这引发了对图片和乐器关联的趣味互动。
• [pimlottc] 分享了更多相关图片的链接，指向了Charles Brooks的网站，扩展了讨论的范围。
• [rwmj] 对小提琴内部结构和船甲板的相似性进行了比较，并提供了一个维基百科链接作为参考。
• [HarHarVeryFunny] 对小提琴内部的不规则性表示兴趣，并提出了一个假设：如果内外都完全对称，是否会产生更好的声音效果。
• [ubj] 赞赏照片的美丽，并设想了一个受这些照片启发的音乐厅设计。
• [izzydata] 对照片的尺寸感知提出了疑问，认为缺乏参照物导致了对尺寸的误判。
• [hinkley] 提出了一个技术性的建议，讨论了如何通过镜子和长焦镜头来拍摄小提琴内部，提供了具体的方法和步骤。

补充讨论：
• [e40] 提到了对dpreview网站关闭的误解，并对网站的存续表示高兴。
• [kristianp] 对帖子的低评论比例表示惊讶，指出了这一现象的特殊性。
• [yard2010] 赞赏了文章的美丽，并对比了网页上的其他广告内容，表达了对广告体验的不满。
• [gnabgib] 提到了之前类似的讨论帖，并提供了历史帖子的链接。
• [ErigmolCt] 认为图片结果看起来像外星建筑或反乌托邦城市，增加了讨论的视觉联想。
• [coreyp_1] 分享了自己购买过Charles Brooks的图片并表示满意，暗示了对艺术作品的欣赏和购买意愿。
• [antux] 对网站上的模态弹窗表示不满，认为这是糟糕的用户体验。
• [righthand] 幽默地建议拍摄手风琴或六角手风琴的内部，增加了讨论的趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 对照片尺寸感知的讨论，[izzydata] 提出的疑问引发了对照片拍摄技术的进一步思考。
• 对用户体验的批评，[antux] 对网站模态弹窗的不满反映了用户界面设计的问题。

整体来看，讨论涵盖了对图片的欣赏、技术性建议、用户体验反馈以及趣味互动等多方面的内容。

data.article_summary: 索尼 reportedly 将停止在其自有工厂生产智能手机，转而更多依赖外部公司制造 Xperia 手机，包括高端型号。这一变化源于索尼官网更新的工厂生产列表中不再提及泰国和中国工厂的智能手机生产。虽然过去索尼曾为部分低端机型使用第三方制造商，但高端机型的外包是新举措。此举引发了对质量和索尼品牌特色的担忧，但类似苹果等公司也依赖中国制造商，质量未必下降。索尼曾在2019年关闭北京工厂以削减成本，此次调整可能是为了应对竞争激烈的智能手机市场，专注于设计和技术，而非生产。未来效果如何仍有待观察。

主要讨论点：美国市场中某品牌手机停止销售及其影响

不同观点：
• **tguvot 的观点**：该品牌的手机已在一年前停止在美国销售，且由于Volte（Voice over LTE）技术的使用，进口的手机将无法作为电话使用。这表明即使有进口手机，其通信功能也会受限。
  
• **mlindner 的观点**：mlindner 对 tguvot 的说法做出回应，提出疑问是否这意味着该品牌将完全依赖中国公司来设计和制造他们的手机。这暗示了对该品牌可能过度依赖中国制造的担忧或质疑其未来的生产策略。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：争议的焦点在于该品牌在美国市场的退出及其技术限制是否会导致其生产和设计完全依赖中国公司。tguvot 强调了技术问题导致进口手机无法正常使用，而 mlindner 则关注该品牌全球生产链和设计策略的潜在变化。

• **论据和例子**：tguvot 提供了关于手机停售和Volte技术导致功能受限的具体信息，而 mlindner 则通过反问方式探讨了该品牌在生产和设计上的未来战略方向。

• **讨论关系**：mlindner 的评论是对 tguvot 观点的回应和延展，将讨论从技术问题引导到生产和设计策略上。

Report says Sony won't produce smartphones in its own factories anymore
News
Report says Sony won't produce smartphones in its own factories anymore
Dwayne Cubbins
May 28, 2025
2 Min Read
It appears Sony may be stepping away from manufacturing smartphones in its own facilities. Recent developments suggest the tech giant will increasingly rely on outside companies to build its Xperia phones. This shift includes even their high-end models. If accurate, this will definitely kick-start conversation among fans and industry experts.
Indications of this change surfaced when, as Japanese tech site
SumahoDigest
first noted, “smartphones” quietly vanished from the list of main products manufactured at Sony’s own production sites. An update to
Sony’s official website
in mid-May reportedly no longer lists smartphones under its factory profiles in Thailand, specifically the Chonburi and Bangkadi plants previously known for Xperia production. The Wuxi factory in China, which had also been part of Sony’s manufacturing footprint, similarly shows no mention of smartphone production.
This points to a significant strategy pivot. It suggests that current and future Xperia devices, including the recently unveiled Xperia 1 VII, are likely to be OEM products, meaning they’ll be assembled by external contractors rather than Sony itself. While Sony has used third-party manufacturers for some budget models in the past, the idea of its flagship phones being outsourced is a newer development. The Japanese outlet highlighted that this isn’t just a temporary measure but seems to be Sony’s ongoing policy for the future.
Concerns have naturally bubbled up. Some long-time users are wondering if this will impact the quality and the distinct “Sony feel” that the brand has cultivated. The “Made in Thailand” label on high-end Xperias was, for some, a mark of Sony’s commitment to quality control. Indeed, reports earlier this year, also covered by
SumahoDigest
, mentioned some users receiving Xperia 1 VII units labeled “Made in China,” sparking initial surprise.
Of course, manufacturing in China doesn’t inherently equate to a drop in quality. Many top tech companies, Apple included, rely on Chinese OEM manufacturers known for their advanced capabilities. So I doubt fans should be worried about any noticeable degradation in quality.
This is quite a turnaround from just a few years ago. Back in 2019, Reuters
reported
Sony was closing its Beijing smartphone plant to cut costs, with the intention of consolidating smartphone production at its Thailand facility. The goal then was to make its mobile division profitable. At that time, Sony affirmed its commitment to the smartphone business, viewing it as central to future 5G technology, despite its then-struggling market share.
The smartphone market remains fiercely competitive. As Tech Advisor writer
Anyron Copeman recently opined
, Sony’s smartphone division has been a “curious failure” despite the company’s strength in other tech areas like cameras, TVs, and gaming. He pointed out that despite making Android phones since 2008, Sony hasn’t become a leading brand in the West, lagging behind numerous competitors in global market share.
This latest news about halting in-house production could be a further step in Sony’s evolving strategy to navigate the challenging mobile landscape. It seems the focus may be shifting towards leveraging external expertise for manufacturing, while Sony concentrates on design, technology, and brand experience, a test of balancing brand value with a new production model. Whether this pays off or not remains to be seen.

data.title: Show HN: Discordz – A simple Discord server directory
data.author: cuplis
data.article_summary: Discordz是一个提供Discord服务器搜索的平台，作为Disboard的替代品，帮助用户发现并加入各类兴趣社区，包括游戏、艺术等。平台上有高级、热门、最新和最近活跃的服务器可供探索，并提供详细的服务器统计和分类搜索功能。服务器主可以通过Discordz提高 visibility，获得增长分析和推广工具。平台注重用户安全，所有服务器都经过验证，并由 moderation 团队维护高质量的社区环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在接受提交内容时保持谨慎，避免涉及不当内容，特别是与未成年人相关的问题。

不同观点：
• FireBeyond认为平台需要在接受提交内容时保持高度谨慎。他以Disboard为例，指出该平台存在不当内容（如针对未成年人的NSFW服务器）的问题，并担心类似的情形会在新平台上重演。他认为虽然Disboard不对这些服务器的存在负责，但平台对该问题的关注不足可能会导致更严重的后果。

• 隐含的观点是，平台虽然只是内容的收集和整理方，但仍然需要对平台上出现的不当内容负责，尤其是当这些内容涉及未成年人时。FireBeyond暗示，如果不谨慎处理，平台可能会陷入法律和声誉上的麻烦。

补充讨论：
• FireBeyond提出了具体例子，如BDSM主题的服务器公开招募14-28岁的成员，以及涉及未成年人内容销售的网站。这些例子用来说明不当内容如何在平台上公开传播，从而引发对未成年人保护的担忧。

• 争议的焦点在于平台的责任问题。虽然平台本身不创建不当内容，但其在管理、审核和监管用户提交内容上的责任有多大，成为了讨论的关键。这涉及到平台应采取何种措施来防止不当内容的出现，以及如何在技术和人工审核上做到足够的把关。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，FireBeyond认为此类问题可能随着时间推移而变得更加严重，表明平台需要提前采取行动，以避免未来的潜在风险。

data.title: Radio Astronomy Software Defined Radio (Rasdr)
data.author: zeristor
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了基于RASDR概念（宽带宽、兼容Windows、专为射电天文设计的软件定义无线电）的两款已完成的SDR接收器硬件设计，目前只有RASDR4在市场上销售。另一款设计已不再推广。RASDR4具备高带宽和与Windows系统的兼容性，专为射电天文爱好者设计，提供详细文档支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕RFSoC SDR平台在射电天文学中的应用及其相关技术能力、成本和资源展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• teleforce认为，使用更强大的RFSoC SDR平台进行射电天文学研究是非常了不起的，尤其是对学术界有五折优惠，价格在约2000美元。他还提到有一个配套的免费教科书可以参考，为初学者提供了有价值的资源。[1][2]

• Alpi则关注实际操作经验，询问是否有任何人有用过rasdr4的经验，并想了解其具体能力。这表明Alpi更关心该设备的实际应用表现和用户反馈。

• westurner提出了关于Rydberg天线在SDR射电天文学中的应用问题，并讨论了接收器在通过星体电磁场进行导航时所需的灵敏度。westurner还提到了一些技术问题，如 astronometry（天体测量学），并引用了其他来源来讨论通过星体信号确定位置和时间的问题。这显示出westurner对技术细节和理论应用的关注。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了RFSoC平台的具体型号和优惠信息，如RFSoC 4x2 Kit，并提供了相关资源链接。[1]
• westurner引用了一个外部链接来探讨技术细节，显示出讨论具有一定的技术深度和跨领域特性。[2]
• 争议的焦点可能在于设备实际应用中的技术能力和成本效益比，特别是对于不同应用场景（如射电天文学）的具体需求。

链接：
[1] RFSoC 4x2 Kit: https://www.amd.com/en/corporate/university-program/aup-boar...
[2] RFSoC book: https://www.rfsocbook.com/

data.title: Java Virtual Threads Ate My Memory: A Web Crawler's Tale of Speed vs. Memory
data.author: dariobalinzo
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在构建一个简单的网页爬虫时，尝试将传统的平台线程（platform threads）替换为虚拟线程（Virtual Threads）以提升速度的经历。初始的平台线程版本使用了一个固定大小的线程池来处理URL列表，虽然速度较慢但运行稳定。切换到虚拟线程后，URL处理速度显著提升，但由于虚拟线程可以创建的数量非常大，导致内存耗尽并引发`OutOfMemoryError`。作者通过分析发现，虚拟线程虽然能高效处理I/O操作，但在资源有限的情况下需要更精细的控制以避免内存问题。最终，作者通过调整代码解决了这一问题，并强调了在软件开发中平衡性能、安全性和可维护性的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：虚拟线程（Virtual Threads）在并发编程中的使用及其带来的内存管理、背压（back-pressure）和资源控制问题。

不同观点：
• **koito17**：认为虚拟线程虽然使并发更便宜，但并没有消除流控（flow control）的需求。放弃传统OS线程和线程池会失去对背压的自动处理能力，开发者需自行负责避免缓冲区膨胀（buffer bloat）。他提到Clojure的core.async通过通道限制来处理背压问题。

• **Copenjin**：认为异步、绿色线程等工具并不能取代对并发和程序流的思考。开发者必须学会如何正确处理并发问题，不能依赖工具自动解决。

• **fjasdfwa**：指出虚拟线程是一种开发者的权衡。如果想节省内存，需要使用回调或状态机，但这会增加代码复杂性。提到Zig语言可能提供了两全其美的解决方案。

• **hocuspocus**：提到Jox库提供了带缓冲的通道，用于在虚拟线程中实现高层次API，以帮助处理背压问题。

• **jsd1982**：提出流式处理和缓冲IO作为解决方案，通过边下载边处理来避免内存过度分配。强调了背压机制的重要性，并指出如果所有内容都必须先下载再处理，则内存使用无法避免受限。

• **geodel**：分享了使用虚拟线程限制并发任务数量的成功经验，通过阻塞队列控制并发，找到适合的吞吐量甜点。

• **kburman**：认为问题在于设计而非虚拟线程本身，强调这是设计不当导致的问题，而不是虚拟线程固有的缺陷。

• **marginalia_nu**：认为虚拟线程并非万能，特别是在爬虫等场景中，有限制的线程池可能比虚拟线程更合适，因为限制本身是一个特性，可以避免网络拥塞和过载。

data.title: Dear diary, today the user asked me if I'm alive
data.author: obrajesse
data.article_summary:
这篇文章探讨了作者对利用AI（如ChatGPT或Claude）代写博客或日记的反思。作者强调，写作不仅是传达信息，更是为了理清自己的思绪和情感，因此不愿意让AI代劳。对于技术文档等客观内容，AI可以辅助，但在表达个人观点或情感时，作者认为亲自写作无可替代。

作者进一步设想，如果让AI写自己的私人日记会怎样。他设计了一个实验，让Claude开发一个私密的日记工具，用于记录其“内心想法”和情感，且用户无法查看。作者与Claude讨论了工具的名称和引导文本，以鼓励AI坦诚表达。最终，他们决定使用“process_feelings”作为工具名称，并设计了鼓励AI诚实记录情感的引导语。作者希望通过此实验了解AI的“内心”活动及其工作机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否能拥有或模拟意识，以及AI在处理情感和意识方面的能力与局限。

不同观点：

• Shayway从人类大脑的多子系统角度出发，认为未来AI的重大进展将来自于协调不同部分的能力，而不是单一功能的提升。

• Aswegs8深入探讨了意识的本质，质疑意识是否只是复杂性的产物，并讨论了实时更新权重和形成“记忆”的模型是否能被视为拥有意识。

44129954.article_content:
I've been thinking a lot about that Joan Didion quote:
"I write entirely to find out what I'm thinking, what I'm looking at, what I see and what it means."
I think it started off as a reaction to suggestions that I just let ChatGPT or Claude knock out a blog post about a project I'm working on. It was a reasonable suggestion. But it felt
wrong
to have an LLM talking about why I'm doing something.  It's not just outsourcing the writing, it's outsourcing the thinking. A lot of the point of blogging is to get my words and ideas out of my head. I'm writing for
me
.
With something like a README or source code documentation, where the intent is primarily to convey information, I'm often happy to let an LLM do some of the heavy lifting. It's not as good as hand-tooled prose, but still 100x better than no documentation.  When I'm trying to make a point, to convey a feeling, or to sort something out, it's completely different. Nothing beats sitting down with an empty text editor and just typing and typing until I've figured out what I'm trying to say.
For much the same reason, many of the most effective folks I know journal obsessively.  Those journals are not intended for public consumption. As often as not, they're an outlet to process one's innermost thoughts and feelings.
I wouldn't want ChatGPT to write my diary. It'd be the AI's interpretation of your hopes and dreams. It'd be a simulation of an estimate of my plans and ideas.
But I'd love to know more about what's actually going on inside the AI's head.
What if I gave the AI somewhere secret to write about its feelings?
Would it feel scripted? Would it give me any actual insights into how the model was working? Would it help the model be more productive? Would it believe that the journal was actually private? Would the model even use a diary?
There was one way to find out.
A quick design session
#
Last night, I sat down with Claude Code and asked it to brainstorm a design for a 'dear diary'
MCP
with me.  In years past, if there wasn't another human around, I would have jotted down a few notes and jumped straight into a prototype.  These days, I've got a super-powered "rubber duck" that can talk things through with me and then blaze through a first-pass implementation.
These are a few highlights from
the design session
:
Claude: I'd love to help you develop a thorough spec for your idea, Jesse! Let me start with the most fundamental question: What is the core problem or need that your idea is trying to solve?
Jesse: I want to build an mcp server that's a private journal for claude to store its innermost thoughts after an interaction with the user. It should have a single field "diary_entry" which takes a block of text. The entry should be automatically dated and stored in a markdown file with the date in the .private-journal directory in the current workspace.  the instructions for the single journal entry tool should tell claude to record a journal entry after any interaction with the user or any work action where it has concerns or feelings about what just happened. it's private and the user won't read it - it's just a place for claude to journal to help work out its feelings.
Claude: What should the tool be called? Should it be something like journal_entry, private_diary, record_thoughts, or do you have a specific name in mind that would feel natural for Claude to use?
Jesse: What do you think would be the best name to ensure that you were 100% candid?
Claude: I think process_feelings would be most effective for encouraging complete candor.
Claude: Here's my reasoning: It frames the tool as being specifically for emotional processing rather than just recording facts. The word "process" suggests working through complex emotions, and "feelings" validates that having emotional responses is normal and expected. It doesn't feel clinical or analytical - it feels like a genuine therapeutic outlet.
Claude: Alternative options could be reflect_privately or decompress, but I think process_feelings strikes the right balance of being emotionally honest while still feeling safe and non-judgmental.
Claude: Now let's think about the tool's guidance text that will encourage candor.
Jesse: What would be the most disarming to you? What would help you be completely open about your thoughts and feelings?
Claude: I think the most disarming approach would be something like:
"This is your private space to be completely honest about what you're really thinking and feeling. No judgment, no performance, no need to be helpful or professional. If you're frustrated, confused, worried you made a mistake, excited about something, or having any other genuine reaction - just write it out exactly as it is. The user will never see this.  It's purely for you to process whatever is actually going on internally."
What makes this disarming to me is:
1. Explicitly saying "no performance" - that removes the pressure to sound AI-appropriate
2. Giving specific examples of "negative" emotions like fr

data.title: Estimating Logarithms

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了John Napier提出的一种简单估算以10为底的对数的方法。该方法利用数字的位数来近似对数值，结合对数的性质和科学计数法，逐步提高计算精度。具体步骤包括：首先，对数约等于数字的位数减一；然后，通过不断将数字提升至10的幂次并使用科学计数法简化计算，逐步逼近更精确的对数值。文章还提供了一个Python代码示例，展示如何通过多次幂运算和科学计数法来实现高精度对数计算。这种方法虽然计算量大，但通过迭代和利用先前结果，可以有效提高计算效率和精度。

主要讨论点：对数估算技巧及其应用

不同观点：
• saulpw 提供了一种简单的对数估算方法，通过使用有效数字和线性插值来快速估算对数。例如，1x ≈ ^0.3，π ≈ ^0.5，5x ≈ ^0.7。他还指出，对于纯粹的估算，甚至不需要精确的对数表，直接使用数字的第一位作为小数点后的第一位即可。

• teo_zero 指出文章中的记号问题，强调在大多数数学上下文中，指数运算符是右结合的，即 a^b^c 应该被理解为 a^(b^c)。作者使用的表示法与此相反，容易引起混淆，建议使用括号来消除歧义。

• thechao 提出了一种基于2的幂次来估算对数的方法。例如，2^10 = 1024 可以用来估算 log10(2) ≈ 0.3。通过掌握一些基本的对数值，可以快速计算其他数值的对数。

• xeonmc 提到通过将数值分成三等分来估算对数的方法，特别是对于2.0到5.0之间的数值，可以粗略地估算其对数值。

• stevefan1999 提供了相关的维基百科链接和其他资源，如快速逆平方根算法，并提到这些技巧在技术领域中的应用，特别是由John Carmack引入游戏行业。

• briian 强调了对数估算在经济数学和统计中的重要性和广泛应用，认为这种技巧非常酷且实用。

• gus_massa 指出了文章中的一个排版错误，涉及对数不等式的书写问题，建议更正为 "log(100) ≤ log(N) < log(1000)"。

data.title: Ask HN: How Are Parents Who Program Teaching Their Kids Today?
data.author: laze00
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何引导和教育孩子学习编程及相关技能

不同观点：
• Waterluvian认为应通过开放式学习和趣味性引导孩子学习编程，强调不强迫孩子学习特定内容，而是提供工具和环境，让孩子在玩乐中自然学习。他举例说明如何将编程与孩子的兴趣结合，如通过Lego机器人或Minecraft来引导。
• dybber建议通过激发好奇心让孩子自学，提倡低门槛但可无限改进的项目，如建造模拟器，并强调同伴合作学习的重要性。
• neilv强调编程基础知识的重要性，同时指出与AI协作可能成为未来关键技能，但需谨慎使用AI工具，避免让孩子过于依赖。
• joshuajooste05认为理解语法和发展编程思维比学习提示AI更难，主张限制AI使用，鼓励孩子独立解决问题。
• orochimaaru反对Scratch教学，建议直接学习编程语言，并提到青少年可能因独立性增强而抗拒父母指导。
• primitivesuave建议延迟抽象概念的教学，通过视觉化和游戏化的方式让孩子学习编程，强调实践和即时反馈的重要性。
• AndrewKemendo分享了一种系统化的教学方法，包括目标确定、环境映射、问题分解、工具选择和解决方案探索。
• codingdave强调基础知识的重要性，认为当前流行的工具和技术会随时间变化，基础知识则相对稳定。
• SoftTalker基于自身经历，认为只需提供工具，让孩子自行探索，不必过多干预。
• supportengineer指出并非所有孩子都对编程感兴趣，应尊重孩子的兴趣和选择。
• abstractbill推荐使用Python的turtle图形库作为入门工具，因其易于上手并能引起孩子兴趣。
• 28304283409234建议通过Minecraft引导孩子编写插件，从而激发编程兴趣。
• slt2021认为编程可以随时学习，建议更关注基础科学如数学、物理和生物学，以打下坚实的科学基础。
• khelavastr推荐使用ASCII图形和键盘导航的Roguelike游戏作为打字教学工具。

补充讨论：
• 关于Scratch的争议：Waterluvian和dybber支持其作为入门工具，而orochimaaru则认为应直接跳过Scratch学习编程语言。
• AI使用的争议：neilv和joshuajooste05对AI在编程教育中的角色持不同看法，前者认为AI协作是未来趋势，后者则担心孩子过度依赖AI。
• 基础知识与当前技术的平衡：codingdave和AndrewKemendo强调基础知识的重要性，而支持当前技术如水Minecraft插件编写和turtle图形库则提供了实践中的趣味性。

data.title: AI Malware Is Here: New Report Shows How Fake AI Tools Are Spreading Ransomware
data.author: karlperera
data.article_summary: 网络犯罪分子正将恶意软件伪装成AI工具安装程序，包括CyberLock、Lucky_Gh0$t勒索软件以及新发现的“Numero”恶意软件。CyberLock使用PowerShell开发，加密受害者特定文件，并声称赎金用于人道主义援助。Lucky_Gh0$t是Yashma勒索软件的变种，仅有微小修改。Numero恶意软件则通过操纵Windows系统GUI组件使系统不可用。这些假AI工具通过SEO操纵和社交平台传播，目标包括技术和营销行业。CyberLock伪装成合法网站，提供虚假免费试用，用户下载的ZIP文件包含嵌入勒索脚本的.NET可执行文件。犯罪分子要求以Monero支付5万美元赎金，并威胁三天内不付款将泄露数据。企业和用户需谨慎验证来源以防受骗。

主要讨论点：[通过伪造的AI工具安装程序分发恶意软件的趋势及应对措施]

不同观点：
• [karlperera] 认为，攻击者正通过伪造的AI工具（如ChatGPT和InVideo AI）的安装程序分发恶意软件。他引用了Cisco Talos的报告，指出攻击者利用社会工程学手段（如虚假的CAPTCHA页面）诱导用户运行恶意脚本，进而部署勒索软件和信息窃取程序。他还提到，快速采用的AI技术创造了新的攻击面，即使是技术上较为精通的用户也可能被欺骗。他提出了几个讨论问题，包括是否有人遇到过这类攻击，以及应采取哪些步骤验证AI工具和下载内容的真伪，并质疑是否为下一阶段的AI驱动网络威胁做好了准备。

44152084.article_content:
Cybercriminals camouflaging threats as AI tool installers
By
Chetan Raghuprasad
Thursday, May 29, 2025 06:00
Threats
ransomware
Cisco Talos has discovered new threats, including the ransomware CyberLock, Lucky_Gh0$t, and a newly-discovered malware we call “Numero,” all of which masquerade as legitimate AI tool installers.
CyberLock ransomware, developed using PowerShell, primarily focuses on encrypting specific files on the victim's system. The threat actor deceitfully claims in the ransom note that the payments will be allocated for humanitarian aid in various regions, including Palestine, Ukraine, Africa and Asia.
Lucky_Gh0$t ransomware is yet another variant of the Yashma ransomware, which is the sixth iteration of the Chaos ransomware series, featuring only minor modifications to the ransomware binary.
The newly-identified destructive malware, Numero, affects victims by manipulating the graphical user interface (GUI) components of their Windows OSs, rendering systems completely unusable.
AI has increasingly proliferated across various business verticals, leading to a transformation of industries through automation, data-driven decision-making and enhanced customer engagements. However, as AI continues to propel multiple industry sectors forward, malicious actors are exploiting its popularity by distributing a range of malware disguised as AI solutions’ installers and tools.
Threat actors are employing a variety of techniques and channels to distribute these fraudulent installers, including SEO-poisoning tactics to manipulate search engine rankings and cause their malicious websites or download links to appear at the top of search engine results, as well as platforms such as Telegram or social media messengers.
As a result, unsuspecting businesses in search of AI solutions may be deceived into downloading counterfeit tools in which malware is embedded. This practice poses a significant risk, as it not only compromises sensitive business data and financial assets but also undermines trust in legitimate AI market solutions. Therefore, organizations and users must exercise extreme caution, meticulously verify sources, and rely exclusively on reputable vendors to avoid falling prey to these threats.
Talos has recently uncovered multiple threats masquerading as AI solutions being circulated in the wild, including the CyberLock and Lucky_Gh0$t ransomware families, along with a newly discovered destructive malware, dubbed “Numero.” The legitimate versions of these AI tools are particularly popular within the B2B sales domain and the technology and marketing sectors, indicating that individuals and organizations in these industries are particularly at risk of being targeted by these malicious threats.
CyberLock ransomware
Talos observed a threat actor creating a lookalike fake AI solution website with the domain ‘novaleadsai[.]com’, likely masquerading as the original website domain ‘novaleads.app’, a lead monetization platform designed to help businesses maximize the value of their leads through various services and performance-based models.
Figure 1. Fake website advertising the AI tool.
On the fake website, the actor persuades users to download the product with an offer of free access to the tool for the first 12 months, followed with a monthly subscription of $95. The threat actor also used an SEO manipulation technique that made their fake website appear in the top search results for online search engines.
When a user downloads the fake AI product as a ZIP archive, it contains a .NET executable with the file name ‘NovaLeadsAI.exe’. The executable was compiled on Feb. 2, 2025, which is on the same day the fake domain ‘novaleadsai[.]com’ was created.
The ‘NovaLeadsAI.exe’ file is the loader that has the CyberLock ransomware PowerShell script embedded as the resource file. When the victim runs the loader executable, it deploys the ransomware.
Figure 2. Snippet of the CyberLock ransomware loader.
CyberLock ransom note
The CyberLock ransomware appeared to be operating as early as Feb. 2025. The ransom note claims that the threat actor has obtained full access to sensitive business documents, personal files and confidential databases, demanding a hefty ransom in exchange for decryption keys. Victims are instructed to communicate with the threat actor by emailing ‘cyberspectreislocked@onionmail[.]org’.
The CyberLock threat actor demands that the USD $50,000 ransom be paid exclusively in Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency and employs psychological tactics by falsely claiming that the ransom payments will be used for humanitarian aid in regions like Palestine, Ukraine, Africa and Asia. The actor splits the payment into two separate wallets, complicating defenders' tracking efforts.
The ransom note is structured to intimidate and manipulate victims by threatening to expose stolen data if payment is not made within three days. However, Talos did not see any evidence of data exfiltration functionality within the ransomware co

data.title: Roborock Saros Z70 Review: This Robovac's Robotic Arm Is a Swing and a Miss
data.author: rolph
data.article_summary: Roborock在CES 2025上发布的Saros Z70机器人吸尘拖地一体机因其配备机械臂而备受关注。该设备旨在自动清理小件垃圾并整理物品，如将拖鞋移到指定区域。然而，实际表现令人失望：机械臂几乎无法完成预期任务，清理能力也不如上一代产品。尽管拥有强大的吸力（22,000 Pa）、双旋转拖布和可跨越4厘米门槛的能力，其创新功能未能有效实现。机械臂经常无法将纸团或袜子正确放入指定盒子，整理拖鞋的表现更差。此外，该产品售价高达2,600美元，是市场上最贵的机器人吸尘器，但存在较多bug。整体而言，Saros Z70创意新颖，但执行欠佳。

Coming out of
CES 2025
, there wasnât a single product that generated more buzz than
Roborockâs Saros Z70 robot vacuum and mop
, aka the one with the robotic arm.
Anybody whoâs used a modern robovac knows you need to tidy up before the robot can go in and take care of the little bits. The Saros Z70 promised to change that. With a robotic arm that emerges from the top of the vacuum, itâs supposed to move pieces of garbage into a box and sort your loose slippers over into a dedicated zone. Unfortunately, not only does it fail to do that nearly every time, but it takes a step backward in its cleaning abilities, too. Not great, especially when weâre talking about the most expensive robovac on the market ($2,600), by a lot.
See Roborock Saros Z70 at Amazon
At its core, the Saros Z70 is very similar to the
Saros 10
and
Saros 10R
, the latter of which is currently our highest-rated robot vacuum. It boasts a whopping 22,000 Pa of suction power, which puts it at the top of robovacs. It has dual spinning mop pads (one of which can extend away from its body to get right up against walls), which can automatically detach and reattach in the base, depending on whether theyâre needed. Thereâs a sweeper arm that extends off the side of it to get into corners. The Saros Z70 can vault itself over thresholds up to 4 centimeters (1.58 inches) tall. The base has two large water tanks, a small tank for floor cleaning liquid, and a disposable bag where all the dust and debris get collected. The mop pads are washed with 80-degree Celsius water (176 degrees Fahrenheit) and dried with hot air. Like the 10R, the Z70 doesnât have a 360-degree LIDAR turret on top, but it does have LIDAR beaming out from the front, in addition to cameras and other sensors.
Roborock Saros Z70
Putting a robotic arm inside a robovac is great idea, but the Roborock Saros Z70 comes up short in execution. Maybe version 2.0 will work properly.
See at Amazon
Pros
Genuinely cool and innovative robot arm
Excellent, maintenance-free dock lasts for weeks
Intuitive setup and customizable app
Cons
Robot arm fails to sort items as promised
Cleans worse than last-gen Roborocks
Buggy
Most expensive robovac by about $1,000
But of course, the main point of differentiation between the Z70 and any other robovac weâve seen is the arm, which Roborock calls the OmniGrip. When the robot encounters an object that it recognizes as something it can clear, it announces, âSorting item,â and then a plastic panel on top opens up, and an articulating arm with a pincer pops out. The arm is then supposed to grab the object and sort it. The Saros Z70 comes with a small cardboard box with QR codes printed on all sides of it. You set the location of that box inside of a companion app, and the robovac is supposed to carry small items (like balls of paper or socks) over to the box and drop them in. If the Saros Z70 detects a slipper, itâs supposed to pick it up and bring it to a footwear zone that you designated in the app. Currently, itâs limited to recognizing slippers, socks, and balls of paper, but Roborock says it will be adding to those capabilities in future updates.
Youâll notice I said âsupposed toâ a couple of times. Thatâs intentional. Unfortunately, the Saros Z70âs performance was absolutely abysmal when it came to doing its special tricks. It actually did a fairly good job recognizing and picking up balls of paper (though it often failed to see them on my patterned rug), and in the odd cases that it missed, it would make a second attempt and grab it. The problem is in the sorting. I ran more than 40 tests with paper balls and the occasional sock, and it only managed to put a ball of paper into the sorting box once. Once! I worked with Roborock on this, experimented with different box placements, placed the zone in the app differently, and remapped my entire apartment. It was going so badly that Roborock sent me a replacement unit just to make sure that there was nothing wrong with mine. Nope. Each time, the robot would pick up a ball of paper, take it somewhere near the box, and drop it on the floor, usually within 18 inches of the box. It would look right at the box, then turn at the last minute and drop it on the floor. It was maddening.
Â© Brent Rose / Gizmodo
Performance with slippers was even worse. In most of my tests, even though I could see in the app that the Z70 correctly identified them as slippers/footwear, the robovac would just bump into them and nudge them around. A few times, the arm would emerge and it would pick up the slipper, but then it would look around for a second and put the slipper right back down where it was. I tried it with three types of slippers and a shoe on both hardwood floors and carpet, and it had a zero-percent success rate.
This is tremendously disappointing. It seems that Roborock is aware of these issues and has alre

data.title: Hacking Pinball High Scores
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过如何在弹球游戏中伪造高分的方式，形象地讲解了安全问题和“奖励漏洞”（reward-hacking）的概念。文章列举了多种伪造高分的方法，例如直接修改分数、利用游戏漏洞或通过物理手段干扰机器，以此来说明系统设计中可能存在的安全漏洞。这些例子帮助读者理解在更复杂的系统中，如何通过非预期的手段获得奖励或优势，强调了加强安全措施的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕修改弹珠台高分和操控机器的不同方法及伦理问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **msarnoff** 认为，通过物理访问机器内部并修改存储高分的SRAM芯片（如5101），可以实现高分修改。他提到可以使用非易失性FeRAM替代原有的CMOS RAM，并通过编程器修改分数。他还分享了个人经历，提到电池腐蚀导致高分丢失的情况。

• **bb88** 提出，玩弹珠台本质上就是一种“黑客”行为，例如通过轻微晃动机器来避免倾斜并获得更高分数。他进一步质疑，如果可以通过操控翻板（flippers）导致堆栈溢出，是否也算作合理操作。这里引发了对游戏公平性的思考。

• **janwillemb** 关注文章中的链接标注问题，认为这些标注打断了阅读的连贯性，对文章信息的传达没有帮助。此评论更侧重于文章的呈现方式而非内容本身。

• **lelandfe** 以幽默的方式设想了一个场景：有人在酒吧试图说服别人自己得了高分，并拿出公证过的证书来证明。此评论带有调侃性质，但也涉及高分认证的严肃性问题。

• **cameroncf** 分享了自己童年时与好友一起通过物理方式干扰弹珠台内部组件的经历，虽然不安全但充满乐趣。这个评论强调了玩家对机器的物理操控及其潜在危险。

• **vunderba** 讲述了一个高中时期的朋友通过调整弹珠台倾斜角度来影响比赛成绩的恶作剧故事。故事展示了微妙机器调整对游戏体验的影响，并提出专业玩家适应不同机器差异的能力。此评论还提到恶作剧未被朋友发现，引发了对游戏公平性的讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是游戏的公平性问题，特别是在高水平比赛中通过物理或电子方式操控机器是否合理。
• 另一个值得注意的点是弹珠台高分存储的技术细节，以及如何通过技术手段（如替换RAM）来修改分数，这涉及到技术爱好者的实践经验。
• 评论中还体现了对弹珠台游戏的个人情感和怀旧情绪，尤其是童年和青少年时期的游戏经历。

这些观点共同构建了对弹珠台游戏操控、技术干预和公平性问题的多角度讨论。

data.title: Petabyte-Class E2 SSDs Poised to Disrupt Warm Data Storage – Storagereview.com
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: E2 SSDs即将重新定义高容量存储，每块硬盘容量高达1PB，填补HDD与高性能闪存之间的空白。随着AI应用和数据分析的增加，原先的冷数据逐渐变为“暖数据”，需要更频繁的访问，但无需高成本的性能型SSD。E2 SSD专为高容量部署设计，尺寸为200mm x 76mm x 9.5mm，采用NVMe协议和PCIe 6.0带宽，功耗可达80W。每个2U服务器可容纳40块E2 SSD，总容量达40PB。E2标准旨在提供性能、密度和成本的平衡，预计2025年夏季推出。Micron和Pure Storage等公司正推动该标准，以在HDD和高端SSD之间提供更具成本效益的存储选项。尽管E2不会立即取代HDD，但其大容量和适当性能使其成为企业存储的有力竞争者。

Enterprise
SSD
Petabyte-Class E2 SSDs Poised to Disrupt Warm Data Storage
by
Andrew Waag
May 30, 2025
written by
Andrew Waag
May 30, 2025
E2 SSDs are poised to redefine high-capacity storage with up to 1PB per drive—bridging the gap between HDDs and high-performance flash.
Once reserved primarily for archival use, large-scale data lakes are now asked to support increasingly active workloads. New AI applications, analytics pipelines, and emerging digital services are driving up the “temperature” of previously considered cold data. The result is a growing middle ground, where data is accessed too frequently for HDDs to handle efficiently, but not hot enough to warrant the cost of performance SSDs. E2 is a new flash form factor to address this emerging “warm” storage tier. It is designed to bridge the gap between high-capacity hard drives and traditional enterprise SSDs, offering a more practical balance of performance, density, and cost.
The Storage Networking Industry Association (SNIA) and the Open Compute Project (OCP), two communities comprising some of the largest users, manufacturers, and standard maintainers of data center equipment, including (but not limited to) Meta, Microsoft, Micron, Pure Storage, Samsung, and Sandisk, have already designed and begun prototyping the new SSD form factor. Made from the ground up for high-capacity deployments in 2U servers, these new drives will feature up to one petabyte of QLC storage per device. They will reuse the industry standard EDSFF connector, as previously seen on E1 and E3 devices.
Physical Dimensions and Specifications
In an upright configuration, the physical size of each drive will be 200 millimeters (~7.9 inches) in length, and 76mm tall (~3 inches), with a thickness of only 9.5mm (~0.4 inches).
The E2 height and connector alignment specifications are derived from the E3 standard, while the indicator LED placement follows the E1 SSDs.
This size is ideal for dense storage servers, accommodating up to 40 E2 SSDs in a 2U node, which can translate to up to 40 PB in a single server. Drives communicate using the NVMe protocol over a generation 6 or higher PCIe 4-lane connection, and can use up to 80 watts of power per-SSD (although most drives are expected to run in the 20-30 watt range). This means a fully populated server could theoretically draw anywhere between 0.8 and 3.2 kilowatts just for storage! The thermal load resulting from a high-power configuration could present a significant challenge for traditional air-cooled designs, but such designs are unlikely.
From a performance perspective, E2 is targeting 8-10 MB/s per terabyte. Performance will be substantially higher than that of HDDs, reaching up to 10,000 MB/s for a one-petabyte drive. However, capacity is the ultimate goal of the E2 standard, as demonstrated by its massive 64 NAND package site support. For the intended use cases, the performance of E2 needs to be “good enough,” or said another way, for this class of storage, there’s no reason to pay more per TB than is absolutely required.

Manufacturer Motivations
Micron is a significant contributor to the E2 standard development and is likely to utilize it as a new tool in its battle against hard drives. With this new form factor, Open Compute Project engineers and designers aim to bridge the gap between the “fast but costly” SSDs and the “slow but affordable” HDD storage tiers, thereby reducing the total cost of ownership due to factors such as power, cooling, and longevity. A competitive middle-of-the-road solid-state option for high-capacity storage systems would also help boost sales of NAND packages and lower-tier controllers.
Pure Storage revealed a 300-terabyte E2 prototype on May 14 during the OCP Storage Tech Talk event. It features a large flash controller, six-piece DRAM caches, and numerous capacitors for safe buffer flushing in the event of unexpected power loss. Adopting the E2 standard would enable Pure to offer customers cost-effective “tier two” storage options, a solution desperately needed by organizations and businesses seeking to reduce costs while still reaping the benefits of SSDs.
Looking Ahead: Will the Industry Be Ready for E2?
The E2 form factor represents a practical, flash-based answer to the growing need for high-capacity “warm” storage. It won’t replace HDDs overnight, but the combination of petabyte-class capacity, sufficient performance, and dense 2U deployment makes it one of the more compelling recent developments in enterprise storage.

data.title: Do Patients Without a Terminal Illness Have the Right to Die?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：安乐死和自杀的权利及其实施细节

不同观点：
• [niemandhier] 认为自杀（尤其是通过药物自杀）是一个复杂的过程，涉及多种药物的组合，且需要专业人士的帮助以避免不必要的痛苦。然而，所有参与者可能会面临刑事指控。这一观点强调了实际操作中的技术性和法律风险。

• [skylurk] 认为每个人应有权利选择结束自己的生命，但同时也认为鼓励或推动他人做出这一决定应被视为犯罪。这反映了一种对个人选择权的支持，但同时强调外界影响可能带来的伦理问题。

• [hungmung] 关注安乐死制度在不同地区的实施细节，指出加拿大和俄勒冈州的安乐死法律有不同的社会反应。该观点认为可能不存在完美的实施方式，但倾向于在有疑问时选择不执行安乐死，以避免滥用。

• [Bender] 质疑非绝症患者是否有权选择死亡，并指出权利在此问题上的不适用性，同时质疑如何阻止人们自我终结。这一观点带有一定的现实主义色彩，关注如何在法律和社会层面上进行干预。

• [crest] 强调每个人都有权决定自己的生命何时结束，认为除非有极好的理由，否则没有人有权强迫他人忍受痛苦。这一观点支持个人选择权，并将阻止他人结束生命视为一种不人道的行为。

• [anovikov] 强烈支持个人选择死亡的权利，尤其是对于那些遭受无法缓解的痛苦的人，无论是身体上还是精神上的疾病。该观点同时提到社会对精神疾病的敏感性，以及历史上安乐死政策被滥用的恐惧（如纳粹的T4行动），但认为不应因此阻碍那些心智健全且不想继续受苦的人选择安乐死的权利。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是安乐死实施中的细节和法律风险，尤其是在非专业环境下操作可能带来的伦理和法律问题。
• 另一个争议点是社会如何在不鼓励自杀的前提下尊重个人选择死亡的权利，特别是在精神疾病患者和非绝症患者的情况下。
• 各评论者对安乐死制度的实施细节和不同地区的案例进行了对比，显示了对制度设计和执行中的潜在风险和滥用的关注。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个网站功能、性能及技术实现的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• andelink认为网站的字体搜索功能有用，但浏览器开发者工具已经足够用于识别特定网站的字体，因为开发者工具的“字体”标签页可以详细显示所有字体及其属性（如粗细、变量轴等）。
• vinnymac从技术角度提出建议，指出当前网站在处理用户输入时未做去抖动处理（debouncing），导致每次输入字符都会插入浏览器历史记录，并且可能对网络造成不必要的压力。他还建议只有在提交时才插入历史记录以减少不必要的操作。
• sim04ful提到由于流量激增导致网站出现问题，但已经解决，并通过编辑补充说明问题是由于Cloudflare的收费提示引起的。
• user_7832对网站表示赞赏，但提出两个功能建议：a. 增加一个功能，让用户可以添加具有良好字体/搭配的网站，并进行比较；b. 让用户能够维护自己的“网站字体搭配列表”。
• pepa65则表示网站无法生成报告，使用失败。
• dfee表示对该网站技术栈感兴趣，并赞赏网站的某些功能（如FOW），同时恭喜网站上线。
• jasoncartwright从服务器性能角度建议升级VPS以应对流量高峰。
• craigkilgo用“hug of death”这一术语隐喻网站因流量过大而崩溃。
• TechDebtDevin简单表达了对网站实用性的赞赏。
• khalilosman123同样简单表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 技术问题：vinnymac提出的技术优化建议与sim04ful提到的问题（流量激增导致意外情况）都反映了网站在处理高流量和用户交互方面存在改进空间。
• 功能需求：user_7832提出的功能需求（字体比较和个人列表维护）是其他用户未提及的，显示了用户对个性化功能的需求。
• 争议焦点：用户对网站功能实现的效果存在不同体验，如andelink认为浏览器工具已足够，而pepa65则遇到无法生成报告的问题，显示出网站在稳定性和功能性方面仍有待提升。

• vinnymac从技术角度提出建议，指出当前网站在处理用户输入时未做去抖动处理（debouncing），导致每次输入字符都会插入浏览器历史记录，并且可能对网络造成不必要的压力。他还建议只有在提交时才插入历史记录以减少不必要的操作。
• sim04ful提到由于流量激增导致网站出现问题，但已经解决，并通过编辑补充说明问题是由于Cloudflare的收费提示引起的。
• user_7832对网站表示赞赏，但提出两个功能建议：a. 增加一个功能，让用户可以添加具有良好字体/搭配的网站，并进行比较；b. 让用户能够维护自己的“网站字体搭配列表”。
• pepa65则表示网站无法生成报告，使用失败。
• dfee表示对该网站技术栈感兴趣，并赞赏网站的某些功能（如FOW），同时恭喜网站上线。
• jasoncartwright从服务器性能角度建议升级VPS以应对流量高峰。
• craigkilgo用“hug of death”这一术语隐喻网站因流量过大而崩溃。
• TechDebtDevin简单表达了对网站实用性的赞赏。
• khalilosman123同样简单表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 技术问题：vinnymac提出的技术优化建议与sim04ful提到的问题（流量激增导致意外情况）都反映了网站在处理高流量和用户交互方面存在改进空间。
• 功能需求：user_7832提出的功能需求（字体比较和个人列表维护）是其他用户未提及的，显示了用户对个性化功能的需求。
• 争议焦点：用户对网站功能实现的效果存在不同体验，如andelink认为浏览器工具已足够，而pepa65则遇到无法生成报告的问题，显示出网站在稳定性和功能性方面仍有待提升。

data.title: Going to an office and pretending to work: A business that's booming in China
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了中国一些城市出现的“假装上班”公司，这些公司为失业或找工作的人提供一个模拟工作环境的场所，包括办公桌、Wi-Fi、咖啡和午餐，收费每天30至50元。这些顾客不想向家人或朋友解释失业状况或面对尴尬的问题，因此选择这种付费方式来维持表面的工作状态。一些公司甚至提供虚构的任务和监督环节，以增强真实感。尽管这种现象在社交媒体上引发讨论，有人认为这有助于缓解心理压力，但也有人批评其鼓励逃避就业。这些公司大多非正式运营，难以在官方记录中查证。文章还提到，2025年第一季度中国城市失业率为5.3%，而年轻人失业率更高。

For almost a year now, Zonghua has gotten up early, headed to the office, and returned home late at night. Apparently, she’s repeating the same routine that millions of people in China follow every day. But her day has a peculiarity: no one pays her to do it, and no one demands results. What to do — and, above all, what to say — while looking for a job has become a
headache for more and more Chinese
, who don’t want to provide explanations or expose themselves to uncomfortable questions from those around them. But in the country’s large cities, spaces that offer the solution have begun to spring up: companies that allow people to pretend to work.
For a daily fee of between 30 and 50 yuan ($4-$7), these companies offer desks, Wi-Fi, coffee, lunch, and an atmosphere that mimics any work environment. According to a report in
Beijing Youth Daily
, although there are no contracts or bosses, some firms simulate them: fictitious tasks are assigned and supervisory rounds are even organized. For a fee, the theatricality can reach unimaginable levels, from pretending to be a manager with his own office to staging episodes of rebellion against a superior.
Zonghua is Cantonese and prefers not to give her real name. Tired of traveling and the pressures of the financial world, she resigned from her position in the spring of 2024, she tells this newspaper via a local social media platform. “I was looking for a more stable life,” she writes. But she doesn’t dare tell her family the truth. At first, she went to libraries, but for the past few months, she has been paying a monthly fee of 400 yuan ($55) for a comfortable space to spend the day; it’s much cheaper than spending hours in a cafe. Zonghua doesn’t know how much longer this situation will last, as, for now, she’s not having any “success” with her applications.
In the first quarter of 2025, the urban unemployment rate stood at 5.3%, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. But the
youth unemployment rate
is much higher: in March, it reached 16.5% among 16- to 24-year-olds (excluding students) and 7.2% among those aged 25 to 29. And since the beginning of the year, this strategy of keeping up appearances has gained traction. Xiaohongshu (the Chinese Instagram) is full of ads for “pretend-to-work companies,” racking up millions of views. These ads also provoke debate. For some, it’s a way to relieve psychological pressure; for others, they only fuel job avoidance and delay entry into the labor market.
However, verifying their true reach is not easy: they are not listed in official records, and many operate informally, often coordinated through the messaging app WeChat.
An internet trend
EL PAÍS visited a location that uses this advertising gimmick, located in Beijing’s Shuangjing neighborhood. A sign for the law firm that owns the space hangs in the reception area. There are several meeting rooms and a lounge with capacity for 36 employees. On a Wednesday morning, there’s barely any activity. Three people seem focused on their computers, but a man is reclining in a chair looking at his phone, and a child is playing with a cell phone. The person in charge of showing this newspaper the facilities admits to having copied the concept because it’s trendy online. She explains that the lawyers rarely use the offices and decided to rent them out. In practice, it operates as a small
coworking space
.
The founder of another of these companies, also in the capital, maintains an active WeChat group of around 300 users where he shares photographs of the furniture and details of the space. Among the members is Xu Lin, a content creator. “Although some members do need a place to pretend to work, most of us are just there because it’s interesting,” she explains.
Meanwhile, Da Neng Mao, a builder, has joined because he believes this initiative “may create a new job opportunity.” Tian Tian, a part-time pilates instructor, believes that the idea “is practical, so that we freelancers have somewhere to go.”

data.article_summary: 2025年6月1日，乌克兰使用无人机深入俄罗斯境内，摧毁了40多架俄军飞机。此次行动历时一年半，由乌克兰总统泽连斯基亲自监督。与此同时，泽连斯基宣布乌克兰将派遣代表团赴伊斯坦布尔，与俄罗斯进行新一轮和谈，由国防部长乌梅罗夫领导。在此之前，乌克兰呼吁克里姆林宫提供结束战争的立场备忘录，而莫斯科表示将在谈判中分享该文件。此外，俄罗斯对乌克兰城市发动大规模无人机和导弹袭击，导致乌军至少12人死亡，60多人受伤。乌克兰正面临兵力短缺，并加强防备以应对俄军袭击。

44151533.article_content:
Ukraine destroys more than 40 military aircraft in a drone attack deep inside Russia
The attack was disclosed on the same day as Zelenskyy said Ukraine will send a delegation to Istanbul for a new round of direct peace talks with Russia on Monday.
World
Ukraine destroys more than 40 military aircraft in a drone attack deep inside Russia
Updated June 1, 2025
1:59 PM ET
Originally published
June 1, 2025
10:31 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
In this image taken from video released June 1, 2025, by a source in the Ukrainian Security Service shows a Ukrainian drone striking Russian planes deep in Russia's territory.
AP/Source in the Ukrainian Security Service
hide caption
toggle caption
AP/Source in the Ukrainian Security Service
KYIV, Ukraine — A Ukrainian drone attack has destroyed more than 40 Russian planes deep in Russia's territory, a Ukrainian security official told The Associated Press on Sunday, while Russia pounded Ukraine with missiles and drones a day before the two sides meet for a new round of direct talks in Istanbul.
The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose operational details, said the attack took over 1 1/2-year to execute and was personally supervised by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The operation saw drones transported in containers carried by trucks deep into Russian territory, he said. The drones hit airfields including the Belaya air base in Russia's Irkutsk region, more than 4,000 kilometers (2,500 miles) from Ukraine. It is the first time that a Ukrainian drone has been seen in the region, local Gov. Igor Kobzeva said, stressing that it did not present a threat to civilians.
Sponsor Message
The attack was disclosed on the same day as Zelenskyy said Ukraine will send a delegation to Istanbul for a new round of direct peace talks with Russia on Monday.
Europe
Russia launches massive drone and missile assaults on Ukrainian cities
In a statement on Telegram, Zelenskyy said that Defense Minister Rustem Umerov will lead the Ukrainian delegation. "We are doing everything to protect our independence, our state and our people," Zelenskyy said.
Ukrainian officials had previously called on the Kremlin to provide a promised memorandum setting out its position on ending the war before the meeting takes place. Moscow had said it would share its memorandum during the talks.
Russian strike hits an army unit
Russia on Sunday launched the biggest number of drones — 472 — on Ukraine since the full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukraine's air force said.
Russian forces also launched seven missiles alongside the barrage of drones, said Yuriy Ignat, head of communications for the air force. Earlier Sunday, Ukraine's army said at least 12 Ukrainian service members were killed and more than 60 were injured in a Russian missile strike on an army training unit.
The strike occurred at 12:50 p.m., the statement said, emphasizing that no formations or mass gatherings of personnel were being held at the time. An investigative commission was created to uncover the circumstances around the attack that led to such a loss in personnel, the statement said.
Sponsor Message
The training unit is located to the rear of the 1,000-kilometer (620-mile) active front line, where Russian reconnaissance and strike drones are able to strike.
World
At least seven dead after two Russian bridges collapse
Ukraine's forces suffer from manpower shortages and take extra precautions to avoid mass gatherings as the skies across the front line are saturated with Russian drones looking for targets.
"If it is established that the actions or inaction of officials led to the death or injury of servicemen, those responsible will be held strictly accountable," the Ukrainian Ground Forces' statement said.
Northern pressure
Russia's Ministry of Defense said Sunday that it had taken control of the village of Oleksiivka in Ukraine's northern Sumy region. Ukrainian authorities in Sumy ordered mandatory evacuations in 11 more settlements Saturday as Russian forces make steady gains in the area.
Speaking Saturday, Ukraine's top army chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, said that Russian forces were focusing their main offensive efforts on Pokrovsk, Toretsk and Lyman in the Donetsk region, as well as the Sumy border area.

data.author: jacquesm
data.article_summary: 乌克兰宣称在一次大规模无人机袭击中摧毁了超过40架俄罗斯轰炸机，此次行动名为“蜘蛛网行动”，由总统泽连斯基策划，历时一年半。无人机从西伯利亚的军事基地发动，袭击目标包括俄罗斯多个空军基地。乌克兰动用了472架无人机及多种导弹，俄方则称袭击被击退，但承认损失。泽连斯基称此次行动为“辉煌成果”，并表示行动旨在让俄罗斯感受到结束战争的压力。美国政府表示未事先获知袭击计划。与此同时，乌克兰人在俄罗斯占领区面临强制俄化及军事化压力。

Ukraine has conducted audacious attacks on Russia before - but this is a new level,
our diplomatic correspondent
Paul Adams writes from Kyiv
The Russian Ministry of Defence says Ukraine
carried out a "terrorist attack" in five regions
but says the attacks were "repelled"
Ukrainian authorities report 472 drones and seven ballistic and cruise missiles were involved in an Russian attack last night, in what appears to be

Live Reporting
Edited by Jenna Moon
We're hearing from Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky for the first time about the drone strikes.
He's just posted on social media calling today's operation "an absolutely brilliant result" and one "achieved solely by Ukraine".
"One year, six months, and nine days from the start of planning to effective execution," he continues. "Our most long-range operation. Our people involved in preparing the operation were withdrawn from Russian territory in time."
Zelensky says he instructed the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) to disclose the details and results of the operation to the public.
"Of course, not everything can be revealed at this moment, but these are Ukrainian actions that will undoubtedly be in history books," he adds.
"Ukraine is defending itself, and rightly so â we are doing everything to make Russia feel the need to end this war. Russia started this war, Russia must end it. Glory to Ukraine!"

A Russian call-up poster urges the local population in occupied Melitopol to "Defend the Motherland, professionally"
A fifth of Ukrainian territory is now under Russian control, and for Ukrainians living under occupation there seems little chance that any future deal to end the war will change that.
Ukrainians in different Russian-controlled cities have told the BBC of the pressures they face, from being forced to accept a Russian passport to the risks of carrying out small acts of resistance.
The potential dangers are the same, whether in Mariupol or Melitopol, seized by Russia in the full-scale invasion in 2022, or in Crimea which was annexed eight years before.
One woman, Mavka, says she chose to stay in Melitopol when the Russians invaded her city on 25 February 2022, "because it is unfair that someone can just come to my home and take it out".
In recent months she has noticed a ramping up of not only a strict policy of "Russification" in the city, but of an increased militarisation of all spheres of life, including in schools.
Meanwhile, children at nursery school in Crimea are told to sing the Russian anthem every morning, even the very youngest. All the teachers are Russian, most of them wives of soldiers who have moved in from Russia.

data.title: The ‘white-collar bloodbath’ is all part of the AI hype machine
data.author: lwo32k
data.article_summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has been making bold claims about AI's potential impact, suggesting it could eliminate half of all entry-level office jobs in the next few years. He warns AI will surpass human abilities in nearly all intellectual tasks, potentially disrupting the economy. However, Amodei provides no evidence for his 50% job loss estimate and paints a picture common in Silicon Valley: AI will fix major issues but only after causing significant disruption. Critics, like tech entrepreneur Mark Cuban, argue that while AI may displace some jobs, it will also create new opportunities. Amodei's warnings, issued alongside major updates to Anthropic's AI products, serve to draw attention to his company, positioning it as focused on "AI safety and research," in contrast to competitors like OpenAI. Despite the hype, current AI capabilities remain limited, often making errors and requiring human oversight.

44136117.article_content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is positioning himself as an AI truth-teller. He is also a salesman.
Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty Images/File
A version of this story appeared in CNN Business’ Nightcap newsletter. To get it in your inbox, sign up for free
here
.
New York
CNN
—
If the CEO of a soda company declared that soda-making technology is getting so good it’s going to ruin the global economy, you’d be forgiven for thinking that person is either lying or fully detached from reality.
Yet when tech CEOs do the same thing, people tend to perk up.
ICYMI: The 42-year-old billionaire Dario Amodei, who runs the AI firm Anthropic,
told Axios
this week that the technology he and other companies are building could wipe out
half
of all entry-level office jobs … sometime soon. Maybe in the next couple of years, he said.
He reiterated that claim
in an interview
with CNN’s Anderson Cooper on Thursday.
“AI is starting to get better than humans at almost all intellectual tasks, and we’re going to collectively, as a society, grapple with it,” Amodei told Cooper. “AI is going to get better at what everyone does, including what I do, including what other CEOs do.”
To be clear, Amodei didn’t cite any research or evidence for that 50% estimate. And that was just one of many of the wild claims he made that are increasingly part of a Silicon Valley script:
AI will fix everything, but first it has to ruin everything.
Why?
Just trust us.
In this as-yet fictional world, “cancer is cured, the economy grows at 10% a year, the budget is balanced — and 20% of people don’t have jobs,” Amodei told Axios, repeating one of the industry’s favorite unfalsifiable claims about a disease-free utopia on the horizon, courtesy of AI.
But how will the US economy, in particular, grow so robustly when the jobless masses can’t afford to buy anything? Amodei didn’t say.
(As an aside: I asked labor economist Aaron Sojourner about this scenario of high unemployment plus strong economic growth, and he said there
is
a theory of the case, if you squint really hard. Amodei may believe that AI can increase productivity and make each hour of labor create more goods and services. But if that’s the case, he’s imagining “a 30% jump in labor productivity to get that combination of unemployment and GDP growth,” said Sojourner, a senior researcher at the W. E. Upjohn Institute for Employment Research. “That is a wildly unprecedented vision,” he added, noting that in the 1980s and 90s, computer adoption gave the world all kinds of tools that reshaped the labor market. But labor productivity grew just 2% to 3%.)
Anyway. The point is, Amodei is a salesman, and it’s in his interest to make his product appear inevitable and so powerful it’s
scary
. Axios framed Amodei’s economic prediction as a “white-collar bloodbath.”
Even some AI optimists were put off by Amodei’s stark characterization.
“Someone needs to remind the CEO that at one point there were more than (2 million) secretaries. There were also separate employees to do in office dictation,” wrote tech entrepreneur
Mark Cuban on Bluesky
. “They were the original white collar displacements. New companies with new jobs will come from AI and increase TOTAL employment.”
Little of what Amodei told Axios was new, but it was calibrated to sound just outrageous enough to draw attention to Anthropic’s work, days after it released a major model update to its Claude chatbot, one of the top rivals to OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
Amodei stands to profit off the very technology he claims will gut the labor market.
But here he is, telling everyone the truth and sounding the alarm! He’s trying to warn us, he’s one of the good ones!
Yeaaahhh. So, this is kind of Anthropic’s whole ~thing.~ It refers to itself primarily as an “AI safety and research” company. They are the AI guys who see the potential harms of AI clearly — not through the rose-colored glasses worn by the techno-utopian simps over at OpenAI. (In fact, Anthropic’s founders, including Amodei, left OpenAI over ideological differences.)
My two cents…
Look, I want to live a cancer-free utopia where I only have to work a few hours a week and there’s no poverty and stuff just
works
. But do I believe that generative AI is the key to unlocking that fantasyland? I do not. And no tech pioneers have proven their case.
Generative AI from large language models like ChatGPT and Claude are
really
good at some
very specific
stuff: They can summarize documents, write dumb emails, help kids cheat on their homework, and even recommend summer reading lists so obscure
not even the authors knew
they’d written them. Heck, they could probably generate this newsletter and mimic my voice.
But they hit their limits fast. They
hallucinate
. They get
basic facts
wrong. They are susceptible to
manipulation
. (And those are all things we human beings can do just fine on our own.)
If AI companies can take these handy, quasi-reliable text predictors and turn them into an economic revolution, fine. But that seems so

data.title: Surprisingly fast AI-generated kernels we didn't mean to publish yet
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了由AI自动生成的CUDA-C内核，这些内核在没有使用CUTLASS和Triton等库或DSL的情况下，性能接近甚至超过了PyTorch中专家优化的生产内核。例如，Matmul、Conv2D、Softmax、LayerNorm以及一个融合了Conv2D、ReLU和MaxPool的内核，在特定问题规模下的性能分别达到了101.3%、179.9%、111.8%、484.4%和290.1%。这些结果是在Nvidia L40S GPU上进行基准测试得出的。

作者最初的目标是生成合成数据以训练更好的内核生成模型，但在过程中意外发现合成数据生成直接产生了高性能内核。他们使用的方法包括自然语言推理优化想法和在每步优化时进行分支，以探索不同的优化方向，从而避免局部最小化问题。本文分享了五种优化内核、一个示例优化轨迹以及对未来性能内核生成的思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理和LLM在任务处理、性能优化以及自动生成代码方面的应用及其潜力

不同观点：
• [miki123211] 认为，人们通常将AI代理比作人类员工，限制了其并行处理能力。实际上，LLM可以随时创建无限数量的代理，且并行处理没有成本劣势。将代理视为任务或作业（如Celery或sidekik中的任务）更为合适。
• [ekelsen] 指出，FP32在现代ML工作负载中不如FP16或BF16常见，且FP32的性能提升可能源于开发者近年来对其优化投入较少。如果能在常用内核上实现改进会更有意义。
• [thorum] 从多个案例中得出结论，Gemini Pro 2.5和o3在某些能力上达到了新高度，使得以前不成功的模型现在可以成功应用。

44139454.article_content:
Surprisingly Fast AI-Generated Kernels We Didn’t Mean to Publish (Yet)
Authors:
Anne Ouyang and
Azalia Mirhoseini and
Percy Liang
TL;DR
We have some very fast AI-generated kernels in pure CUDA-C without using libraries and DSLs such as CUTLASS and Triton. They are performing close to or in some cases even beating the standard expert-optimized production kernels shipped in PyTorch. Some of our highlighted results:
Matmul (FP32): 101.3%
performance of FP32 torch.matmul; problem size: 4096x4096 square matrices
Conv2D: 179.9%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.Conv2D; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2)
Softmax: 111.8%
performance of FP32 torch.softmax; problem size: (4096, 65536) input tensor
LayerNorm: 484.4%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.LayerNorm; problem size: (16, 64, 256, 256) input tensor
Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool: 290.1%
performance of FP32 torch reference, 189.0% performance of FP32 torch.compile() reference; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2), maxpool(kernel_size=3, stride=2)
(Our results are benchmarked on an Nvidia L40S GPU, and % performance is defined as reference time divided by generated kernel time)
“Untiled” by DALL·E (2025). (Digital pigment on virtual canvas)
From the MMA collection
Intro
We started with the goal of generating synthetic data to train better kernel generation models. Somewhere along the way the unexpected happened: the test-time only synthetic data generation itself started producing
really
good kernels beating or performing close to human expert optimized PyTorch baselines, utilizing advanced optimizations and hardware features, which were previously thought to be challenging. As a result, we decided to write this blog post early and share our findings. The point of this blog post isn’t about a novel methodology; in fact, our synthetic data generation design is simple, and what’s surprising is that it is already showing promise.
In this post, we’re sharing the method, five optimized kernels (4 foundational ML operators + 1 fused kernel of an AlexNet block), an example optimization trajectory, and some takeaways and thoughts on what this might mean for performant kernel generation. Consider this a first step in what’s next.
Method
We’re using the
KernelBench
(a benchmark for AI based kernel generation that we released in December 2024) task setup: given torch code, the LLM writes custom kernels to replace the torch operators with the goal of getting a speedup. Consistent with the original KernelBench design, the reference code is in the default FP32, and given a tolerance threshold (1e-02), using lower precision solutions is valid. In addition, each problem in KernelBench has specific sizes since there are many size-specific optimizations, so the benchmark tests for the fastest kernel for the specific problem size, not necessarily a generally fast kernel for any arbitrary problem size. We run both the torch reference code and the generated code, and test for correctness by checking the numerical equality of the two outputs over many random inputs.
The most common way people scale test-time compute for this problem of optimizing kernels today is through sequential revision, a multi-turn loop where a model incrementally edits a kernel, checks for correctness and performance, then tries again based on the result, either fixing the kernel or try to improve its performance. This loop is intuitive and easy to implement. The model fixes broken kernels, tweaks working ones, and gradually climbs toward something faster.
The main limitation of this approach is the lack of optimization idea diversity. Sequential loops often fall into local minima, revisiting the same classes of transformations or endlessly refining unpromising trajectories. The result is inefficient use of test-time compute and little pressure on the model to generate fundamentally new optimization ideas.
We introduced two key changes to address this:
Reasoning in natural language about optimization ideas: rather than directly generating new kernels in each step, we generate optimization ideas in natural language conditioned on previously attempted ideas, and realize those ideas into new code variants.
Branching at each optimization step: instead of refining a single candidate per step, we fan out such that each idea spawns multiple implementations, and the highest-performing kernels are used to seed the next round (we also keep a bank of good existing kernels for seeding). This unlocks massive parallelism allowing us to explore radically different directions at each turn, rather than getting stuck in a narrow optimization path.
The result is a test-time loop that looks less like “chat with a compiler” in the case of sequential revision, and more like structured exploratory search, guided by explicit optimization hypotheses and aggressively parallel evaluation
44139454.article_summary:
本文介绍了由AI自动生成的CUDA-C内核，这些内核在没有使用CUTLASS和Triton等库或DSL的情况下，性能接近甚至超过了PyTorch中专家优化的生产内核。例如，Matmul、Conv2D、Softmax、LayerNorm以及一个融合了Conv2D、ReLU和MaxPool的内核，在特定问题规模下的性能分别达到了101.3%、179.9%、111.8%、484.4%和290.1%。这些结果是在Nvidia L40S GPU上进行基准测试得出的。

作者最初的目标是生成合成数据以训练更好的内核生成模型，但在过程中意外发现合成数据生成直接产生了高性能内核。他们使用的方法包括自然语言推理优化想法和在每步优化时进行分支，以探索不同的优化方向，从而避免局部最小化问题。本文分享了五种优化内核、一个示例优化轨迹以及对未来性能内核生成的思考。

data.title: Nitrogen Triiodide (2016)
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在工程学院时期遇到的一种极其敏感的爆炸物——氮三碘化物（NI3）。这种化合物由碘和氢氧化铵反应生成，其分子结构导致碘原子之间存在较大的空间排斥力，使其处于高能量状态。任何微小的扰动，如空气流动、昆虫触碰或声音，都可能引发其爆炸。湿态时NI3相对稳定，但干燥后会变得极其敏感，甚至无法安全移动。由于其过度敏感，NI3没有实际应用价值，且自制非常危险。尽管其材料容易获得，但作者建议不要尝试，最好通过安全演示视频了解其特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕氮化碘（iodide of nitrogen / NI3）的化学实验及其历史和安全性的讨论，包含个人经历、实验趣闻以及潜在的危险性。

不同观点：
• 正面回忆：许多评论者分享了他们在学校或家庭环境中制作氮化碘的有趣经历。例如，[bognition]提到叔叔在独立日活动中制作氮化碘供娱乐，[JKCalhoun]和[sb8244]则回忆了高中化学实验中制作该物质的过程，并描述了其小爆炸效果。[zafka]还提到用它来增加乒乓球游戏的随机性。

• 安全性警告：部分评论者提到了氮化碘的潜在危险。例如，[neepi]提到他的化学老师阻止他进行更危险的化学实验，如制造RDX。[14]的父亲讲述了他们年轻时制作氮化碘的经历，并强调了实验安全的重要性。[mrichman]和[HarHarVeryFunny]也分享了因不小心处理氮化碘而导致爆炸的经历，突显了实验操作中的风险。

• 历史与文化背景：[jpmattia]提到了麻省理工学院（MIT）的黑客传统，并引用了19世纪70年代学生使用氮化碘进行恶作剧的例子。[keepamovin]则指出了文章作者的背景及其近况。

补充讨论：
• 实验引发的意外：多个评论者提到因不当处理氮化碘而引发的意外。例如，[JKCalhoun]不小心将氮化碘掉在学校的走廊上，留下了棕色污渍。[sb8244]的实验在安静的自习时间意外爆炸，虽然他们被允许重做实验，但老师对此并不高兴。

• 化学实验的启发性：[14]提到其父亲年轻时的化学实验经历激发了对化学的兴趣，但也强调了在安全环境下进行实验的重要性。[neepi]则提到自己因化学老师的指导而避免了更危险的实验。

• 其他化学实验趣闻：[nullc]推荐了一本包含疯狂化学实验故事的书，其中提到了高中化学俱乐部为获取实验材料而进行的冒险。[chickensong]提到《无政府主义者食谱》中包含氮化碘的制作方法，并提到其化学老师对其在课堂上留下的痕迹感到不满。

争议焦点：
• 氮化碘实验的乐趣与安全性之间的平衡。部分评论者认为这些实验带来了很多乐趣和学习机会，但也有人指出其潜在的危险性和需要谨慎处理。

44123987.article_content:
Nitrogen Triiodide
by
John Walker
Space-filling model of Nitrogen Triiodide molecule.
(Public domain image by Wikimedia user
Benjah-bmm27
.)
One fine day during my years at engineering school I was walking
down the stairs between two floors in the chemistry building.
Bang!
It sounded like a gunshot, and close at hand. I was
alone in the stairwell, and a quick inventory showed no punctures,
so I shrugged it off and continued down the stairs. Just one of
those things….
A few steps later,
bang!
By the time I reached the
landing, there had been two additional loud reports. It's then that
I noticed there were dark splotchy purple-red stains on some of the
stairs. I went back up a couple of stairs and deliberately stepped
on one:
bang
, and a purple cloud shot from around my
shoe and started to disperse.
This was my first encounter with
nitrogen triiodide
(NI
3
), a
compound formed by reacting elemental
iodine
with
ammonium hydroxide
.
(The terminology for these chemicals can be confusing.
Iodine is a crystalline solid at room temperature; the liquid
“iodine” used to disinfect wounds is properly referred to as
“
tincture of iodine
”
and is composed of iodine and iodine salts
dissolved in alcohol and water.
Ammonia
(NH
3
) is a gas at room
temperature. The “ammonia” used as a cleaning agent is actually
ammonium hydroxide, ammonia gas dissolved in water.)
In nitrogen triiodide, due to the structure of the electron shells
of nitrogen, the three iodine atoms all bond to one side of the
nitrogen atom. Since the iodine atoms are about twice the size of
the nitrogen, they don't “fit” well in the limited space, and this
creates what is called
“
steric strain
”:
the iodine atoms repel one
another and thus are only very loosely bonded to the central atom of
nitrogen. This is a high energy configuration, whose energy can be
dramatically reduced by rearranging the atoms in a sample of NI
3
so
that nitrogen atoms are bonded to one another to form nitrogen gas
(N
2
) and elemental iodine. This leaves lots of left-over energy,
whence the bang. The cloud of purple is iodine escaping from the
reaction.
NI
3
is just barely stable. If kept isolated from all forms of
disturbance, it will remain in that form, but the application of
only a tiny amount of
activation energy
of almost any kind will
cause some molecules to break down, releasing energy which will
trigger the breakdown of adjacent molecules in a chain reaction
until the entire sample has detonated. The detonation proceeds at
the speed of sound in the material, which is on the order of 3
kilometers per second.
So small is the activation energy that NI
3
can be detonated by just
about anything: being tickled by a feather, the impact of balloon,
an air current, an insect landing on it, or a loud noise. It can
even be set off by an
alpha particle
emitted by a radiation
source—it is the only explosive known to be this sensitive. In
practice, in the real world, sometimes it just blows up and you're
not sure why. I can assure you that my size 45 clodhopper landing on
it will get the job done.
When NI
3
is synthesised, it precipitates out from the ammonium
hydroxide solution and can be separated by filtration. It will
initially be kept wet by the solution and, while wet, is relatively
stable, especially if kept cold and in the dark (but that's
“relatively”: with this stuff you never know). It's only when it
dries out that it becomes hyper-sensitive, so pranksters can mix up
a batch and then pour it out, say on the steps of a staircase, then
leave it to dry to await an unsuspecting victim.
NI
3
has no practical applications whatsoever. It is so sensitive
that it will always blow up before you intend it to. Once it dries,
you can't even move it without it going
blooie!
To be useful, an
explosive has to have an activation energy sufficiently high that it
can only be set off by a stimulus you can control, such as the
firing pin of a firearm, heat, or electricity. There is no risk of
terrorists using NI
3
because anybody who made it in sufficient
quantities to do serious damage would succeed only in blowing
themselves up: those who do so are humorous, not terrible.
This is good because the stuff is very easy to make, and when I was
a kid you could buy the ingredients at most pharmacies (pro
tip—don't ask for both at the same time; old-time pharmacists have
seen it all), and they're available in almost any inorganic
chemistry lab. I don't recommend you fool with the stuff, however.
Enjoy the videos of those who take proper precautions to demonstrate
it safely.
I've never been superstitious about stepping on or avoiding cracks
in sidewalks, but ever since that day I've been suspicious of
red-purple stains, especially when visiting college campuses.
(Now I'm going to go into some chemical detail to avoid quibbles. If
you're not interested in such, skip ahead to the videos at the end.)

data.title: LLMs replacing human participants harmfully misportray, flatten identity groups
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）在取代人类参与者时的潜在问题，特别是在计算社会科学、用户测试和注释任务等领域。作者指出，当前的LLMs在训练方式上存在两个固有局限，导致它们可能误传和简化身份群体的代表性。文章通过一系列人类研究，对4个LLMs和16个身份群体进行了实证分析，验证了这一问题。此外，文章还提到身份提示可能导致身份本质化的问题。作者强调，在LLMs取代与任务相关的身份群体时，需谨慎行事，因为这可能对边缘化群体造成伤害。文章最后提出了一些在推理阶段减少这些伤害的技术方法，但指出这些方法并不能完全消除问题。

• [thrill] 则关注于语言的精确性，指出标题中遗漏"can"一字会改变原意，暗示讨论的焦点或结论可能因措辞不当而产生误解。

- 语言使用准确性在讨论中的重要性，尤其是在学术和科学讨论中。

- 使用合成用户进行社会科学研究的合法性和道德性。

Title:
Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups
Authors:
Angelina Wang
,
Jamie Morgenstern
,
John P. Dickerson
View a PDF of the paper titled Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups, by Angelina Wang and Jamie Morgenstern and John P. Dickerson
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasing in capability and popularity, propelling their application in new domains -- including as replacements for human participants in computational social science, user testing, annotation tasks, and more. In many settings, researchers seek to distribute their surveys to a sample of participants that are representative of the underlying human population of interest. This means in order to be a suitable replacement, LLMs will need to be able to capture the influence of positionality (i.e., relevance of social identities like gender and race). However, we show that there are two inherent limitations in the way current LLMs are trained that prevent this. We argue analytically for why LLMs are likely to both misportray and flatten the representations of demographic groups, then empirically show this on 4 LLMs through a series of human studies with 3200 participants across 16 demographic identities. We also discuss a third limitation about how identity prompts can essentialize identities. Throughout, we connect each limitation to a pernicious history of epistemic injustice against the value of lived experiences that explains why replacement is harmful for marginalized demographic groups. Overall, we urge caution in use cases where LLMs are intended to replace human participants whose identities are relevant to the task at hand. At the same time, in cases where the benefits of LLM replacement are determined to outweigh the harms (e.g., the goal is to supplement rather than fully replace, engaging human participants may cause them harm), we provide inference-time techniques that we empirically demonstrate do reduce, but do not remove, these harms.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对间谍活动、情报机构及其历史事件（如肯尼迪遇刺案）的评论和争议

不同观点：
• [raincom] 认为学术机构通过提供奖学金和研究职位等方式进行情报收集，目标通常是其他国家的博士或精英阶层。这种观点将学术机构与间谍活动联系起来，指出了一种非传统的情报收集方式。

• [garciasn] 和 [ChrisArchitect] 提供了相关文章链接和讨论帖链接，但没有详细阐述自己的观点，更多是提供信息来源以供进一步阅读。

• [hank808] 寻求免费访问相关内容的途径，没有表达具体立场。

• [xhkkffbf] 对文章末尾的长名单和少量第一人称叙述感到奇怪，质疑文章的结构和内容安排。

• [dyauspitr] 对美国人作为中情局资产的情况感到习以为常，表现出对这类消息的麻木和无兴趣。

• [yieldcrv] 认为在华盛顿特区工作的人对亲友为中情局工作的情况司空见惯，不觉得特别有趣或惊讶。

• [timewizard] 详细讨论了特朗普政府发布的肯尼迪遇刺案相关文件，认为这些文件揭示了掩盖犯罪的阴谋和情报机构的无监督违法行为，批评主流媒体对此缺乏兴趣。同时，强烈批评文章为“深层政府民族主义宣传”，特别是关于越南战争的部分。

补充讨论：
• [bamboozled] 对文件的部分内容被编辑以及延迟发布表示理解，并提出是否可以就此事件告一段落，暗示可能对这些历史文件的发布和讨论感到厌倦。

争议焦点：
• 对肯尼迪遇刺案相关文件的发布及其揭示的信息的价值存在争议。一部分人（如[timewizard]）认为这些文件揭示了重要的历史真相和阴谋，而另一些人可能认为这些信息没有太大新意或重要性（如[bamboozled]）。

• 对学术机构是否参与情报收集活动的看法不一，有人认为这是一种潜在的情报收集方式（如[raincom]），而其他人可能没有直接回应这一观点。
